Source slide page 3 (extracted text):
ENGINEERING CHEMISTRY 
Functional materials - Polymers

Polymer composites
Materials made from two or more constituent materials and their properties are not attainable by any individual component alone are called composites 

When one or more of the components are polymers they are called polymer composites

Two components are fibre and matrix
matrix: polyester, epoxy, phenolic, silicone, melamine, vinyl derivatives
fibers: glass fiber, boron filaments, carbon/graphite fibers, aramid (aromatic polyamide), aluminum fiber 

Polymer composite are produced by suitably bonding a fiber material with a polymer resin matrix and curing the same under pressure and heat

Composites have high strength / unit weight

[00:00:00.772] Hello everyone, welcome back to this course on engineering chemistry. We will continue with module seven on functional materials on polymers, and in today's class we are going to study about polymer composites.
[00:00:17.156] We will look at Kevlar synthesis properties and applications and then we will study about reinforced Kevlar composites. Firstly, let us understand what is a composite.
[00:00:32.100] In a composite we will have two or more constituent materials
[00:00:37.604] and their properties are not attainable by each of these components acting alone. It's only when they are mixed together and form a single material that is known as a composite.
[00:00:54.148] Now what would be a polymer composite? When one or more of these components are polymers, we call them as polymer composites. So what are the two components? There is always a fiber and a matrix. The matrix would be
[00:01:09.776] Polyester, epoxy, phenolic, silicone, melamine, or a vinyl derivative. And the fiber could be a glass fibre, boron filaments, carbon, graphite fibers, aromate, that is aromatic polyamide, or aluminium fibre. So
[00:01:27.312] With these two components, the material which is made is known as the polymer composite.
[00:01:34.276] Now how do we produce them? They are produced by suitably bonding the fibre material with the polymeric coalescent matrix and curing the same under pressure and heat.
[00:01:48.592] Now why are these composites so popular? Because they have very high strength per unit weight. So that makes them very useful materials for a variety of applications.
[00:02:07.012] Let us study about Kevlar, which is a very important fibre. It is no it is an aromate fibre. What do we mean by aromate fibre? It is aromatic.
[00:02:19.588] polyamide. Now the chemical name for this would be polyparaphenylin pterythalamide. Now how does it get that name?
[00:02:30.832] It is because of the components which are being used, because of the monomers which are being used to make the polymer. Now it is a condensation polymer.
[00:02:43.684] Condensation of two monarchs that is one for phenyline diamine and one for benzene di carbone fluoride. Now one for benzene di carbide chloride is basically coming from thalic acid. So we know that thalic acid, this is thalic acid, teri thalide.
[00:03:01.456] thalic acid because these are in the para position the COOH COH groups are in the parapositions so we call it as steal acid and instead of the thalic acid we are using the acid chloride so this becomes steady thaloal chloride.
[00:03:17.040] That is because the reactivity will be much more enhanced when we use the teritaloid fluoride. Now what is the other monoma being used? It is 14 phenyline dye.
[00:03:29.648] Now that also would be para-phenylin diamine. Again, these two are in the para position. The amine groups are in the para position. So we have an NH2 here, NH2 here, and we have COCL, COCL. So as expected between the two monomers, we have this condensation.
[00:03:48.484] polymerization which will take place, the condensate condensation reaction would
[00:03:53.616] Result in elimination of an HCl molecule. So we can see very clearly when HCl is eliminated from here, we are going to get a CONH linkage, and that is known as the amide linkage. So like this, these two monomers are because they have
[00:04:11.344] Two functional groups each. So if this condensation happens, this side is still open for the next uh diamine to attach, and similarly this NH2 is open for the next.
[00:04:24.064] COCL group to attach. So therefore the polymerization continues this way, and what we get is amide linkages between these monomers and we get Keblar. So this polymer is known as Keblar. How did we get it? It is a condensation polymer.
[00:04:43.556] Now let us see why Kevlar is such a strong material. Kevlar is known to be five times stronger than steel on an equal weight basis. Equal weight.

[00:11:50.480] So it absorbs moisture, hence moisture resistant substituents have to be added inside to make it as less hygroscopic as possible. Now what we discussed so far is about the Keblar fiber.
[00:12:09.540] We have still not formed the composite because when we talk of a composite, we know there are two components. So Kepler fiber itself has so much strength. Now if this is made into a composite, so how will we make it into a composite? Obviously, we need a
[00:12:27.632] uh matrix for that and that matrix is usually an epoxy resin. So it is made by combining the blad fiber with the epoxy resin matrix. And now the material will become so strong that it is going to
[00:12:45.296] now have many more applications. So what is the use of making a composite like this? This matrix matrix when you have and these fibers are embedded in it, then any force which is applied onto the
[00:13:01.264] uh material will be dissipated the the impact is going to be taken by the metric so that makes the material even more strong. So what would be now applications of such a material? This is known as reinforced Kevlar composites.
[00:13:17.136] Now here we have we can make monocope bodies of Formula One racing cars, helicopter rotor blades, kayaks.
[00:13:25.056] tennis and tennis and squash rackets. So now the applications have increased because the material is still more stronger as compared to Kepler. So this is about
[00:13:38.976] Kevlar on the next class we will talk of another polymer composite and that is carbon fiber. Thank you.
